ns2:group.ns2:title: Is Australia’s Foreign Policy Being Led by a Tabloid? The Truth About ASPI
ns2:group.ns2:description:
In this video, I expose credibility issues at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI), which, in my opinion, operates more like a tabloid than a legitimate think tank. My goal is to inform China-focused journalists, policy researchers, and Australian taxpayers about ASPI’s questionable research practices.
Many policy experts in the U.S., Australia, and Europe already question ASPI’s credibility, yet mainstream journalists continue to treat it as a reliable source. I believe ASPI disguises clickbait reports as serious research, shaping public discourse under the guise of expertise.
ASPI’s report Singing from the CCP Songsheet prominently features me, selectively highlighting a few of my COVID-related videos to frame me as ‘propaganda.’ In my view, this is cherry-picking—ignoring my hundreds of non-COVID videos and the real reason for my content shift: pandemic restrictions preventing food and travel filming.
Key Issues in this video:
🔴 Guilt by Association – ASPI cites my appearances on Chinese state media as “propaganda” while ignoring that Former U.S. Ambassador Max Baucus and current Australian Ambassador (Former PM) Kevin Rudd have done the same.
🔴 Poor Research – ASPI includes an influencer funded by the U.S. State Department in their report about “Chinese propaganda,” missing their own contradiction—likely due to their lack of expertise in China and Chinese social media.
🔴 Deleted Citations – ASPI initially cited U.S. State Department funding for a report, then deleted the reference, blaming a “website upload issue.” What kind of legitimate think tank could make this kind of mistake?
Watch to see how ASPI misleads the public with flawed research and misleading narratives.
